cards.b: A measure of the quantity of matter in an object. Unit kg, scalar, same everywhere.
The gravitational force on an object that has mass. Unit N, vector, changes with g.
Gravitational force per unit mass: g = W ÷ m. About 9.8 N/kg on Earth.
W = mg (W in N, m in kg, g in N/kg).

cards.f: Which instrument measures mass and which measures weight?
cards.b: Mass: balance. Weight: force meter (newton meter).
ρ = m ÷ V; kg/m³ or g/cm³. Water is 1000 kg/m³ = 1.0 g/cm³.

cards.f: Find the volume of an irregular solid that sinks
cards.b: Displacement: V = final reading − initial reading in a measuring cylinder (or collect overflow from a displacement can).

cards.f: When does an object float in a liquid?
cards.b: When its density is less than the density of the liquid.

cards.f: Newton's first law (in the notes' words)
cards.b: With no resultant force, an object stays at rest or continues in a straight line at constant speed.
The resultant force (N) on the object. Acceleration is in the same direction as the resultant force.
Force between two surfaces that may impede relative motion and produces heating.
Force per unit extension: k = F ÷ x (N/m). It is the gradient of a load–extension graph (load on y-axis).
The point beyond which extension is no longer proportional to load; the graph stops being a straight line.

gaps.s: Weight is the gravitational ___ on an object that has mass.
Gravitational field strength on Earth is about ___ N/kg.
A 5.0 kg mass on Earth has a weight of ___ N.
A block of mass 200 g and volume 50 cm³ has a density of ___ g/cm³.
A resultant force of 12 N acts on a 3.0 kg trolley, giving an acceleration of ___ m/s².
A spring extends by 0.050 m when a force of 10 N is applied. Its spring constant is ___ N/m.
An object sinks in a liquid if its density is ___ than that of the liquid.
The unit of the spring constant is newtons per ___ .

short.q: Describe how to find the density of an irregular stone that sinks in water.
short.model: Measure mass on a balance. Find volume by displacement in a measuring cylinder (final − initial reading). Calculate density = mass ÷ volume.
points: volume by displacement of water (V₂ − V₁)

short.q: An astronaut has mass 70 kg. Calculate her weight on the Moon where g = 1.6 N/kg. State what happens to her mass.
short.model: W = mg = 70 × 1.6 = 112 N. Her mass stays 70 kg.

short.q: A 1200 kg car has a driving force of 3000 N and a drag force of 1000 N. Calculate its acceleration.
A load–extension graph for a spring is straight then curves. Explain what the straight part and the point where it curves show.
short.model: In the straight part extension is proportional to load. The curve starts at the limit of proportionality, after which extension is no longer proportional.
points: straight line through origin: extension ∝ load
curve begins at limit of proportionality

short.q: Oil (density 0.80 g/cm³) is poured onto water. State and explain which liquid forms the bottom layer.
short.model: Water forms the bottom layer because its density (1.0 g/cm³) is greater than that of the oil, which floats on top.
points: water has the greater density / oil less dense so floats
